'''John D. Joannopoulos''' (April 26, 1947 – August 17, 2025) was an American physicist, focused in condensed matter theory. He was the Francis Wright Davis Professor of Physics at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], an Elected Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS), an Elected Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (AAA&S), and an Elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) and [[American Physical Society]] (APS).

==Life and career==
Joannopoulos was born on April 26, 1947, in New York City to [[Greeks|Greek]] parents.<ref name="aip-history">[http://history.aip.org/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?joannopoulosj Array of Contemporary American Physicists listing]</ref> He is the recipient of numerous awards and honors. Most recently, in 2015, the [[Optical Society of America]] (OSA) awarded him the [[Max Born Award]] and the APS awarded him the [[Aneesur Rahman]] Prize for Computational Physics, both significant awards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellow/joannopoulos-john |title=John Joannopoulos |publisher=aaas.org |accessdate=May 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180524004516/https://www.aaas.org/fellow/joannopoulos-john |archive-date=May 24, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://web.mit.edu/physics/people/faculty/joannopoulos_john.html |title=John Joannopoulos |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=May 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://isnweb.mit.edu/joannopoulos.html |title=John Joannopoulous |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=May 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180531103155/http://isnweb.mit.edu/joannopoulos.html |archive-date=May 31, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ab-initio.mit.edu/about.html |title=Lab |publisher=mit.edu |accessdate=May 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>[https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Joannopoulos&first_nm=John&year=2015 American Physical Society article on Joannopoulos getting prize]</ref>

Joannopoulos was appointed director of the Institute for Soldier Nanotechnologies in 2006,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://isnweb.mit.edu/joannopoulos.html |title=Institute for Soldier Nanotechnologies bio of Joannopoulos |access-date=2017-05-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180531103155/http://isnweb.mit.edu/joannopoulos.html |archive-date=2018-05-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and was a Principal Investigator at the [[Research Laboratory of Electronics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=John D. Joannopoulos » MIT Physics |url=https://physics.mit.edu/faculty/john-joannopoulos/ |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=MIT Physics |language=en-US}}</ref>

Joannopoulos had been on the MIT faculty since 1974. He held his BA and PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, the latter received in 1974. His doctoral studies, advised by [[Marvin L. Cohen]], focused on electronic structure of complex crystalline and amorphous semiconductors.<ref name="aip-history"/>

Joannopoulos had helped set the theoretical foundations of key computational techniques for realistic and microscopic studies of complex materials systems, including the electronic, vibrational, and optical structure of crystalline and amorphous solids, their surfaces, interfaces, and defects; localization in disordered systems; and the first ab-initio studies of [[phase transition]]s and critical phenomena. In the early nineties, he also helped spawn the development of a new class of materials ([[photonic crystal]]s) that provide new mechanisms to control the flow of light and have revolutionized the fields of optical and lightwave physics.<ref name="mit_obituary"/>

His former students include Nobel Laureate [[Robert B. Laughlin]], along with professors [[Yaneer Bar-Yam]], [[Shanhui Fan]], [[Steven G. Johnson]], [[Eugene J. Mele]], [[Michelle Povinelli]], [[Karin M. Rabe]], [[David Vanderbilt]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ab-initio.mit.edu/people.html |title=Members of the Ab-Initio Physics Research Group |access-date=2024-05-02}}</ref> and many other faculty at major universities.<ref name="mit_obituary"/>

Joannopoulos died on August 17, 2025, at the age of 78.<ref name="mit_obituary">{{cite news |last1=Chu |first1=Jennifer |title=Professor John Joannopoulos, photonics pioneer and Institute for Soldier Nanotechnologies director, dies at 78 |url=https://news.mit.edu/2025/professor-john-joannopoulos-dies-0819 |access-date=19 August 2025 |work=MIT News |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=19 August 2025}}</ref>
